is.t: AiForm vs. B1SA/B1LINK, MineVendorHub, SCNet | Prepared 22 August 2026

This workbook supports a go/no-go decision on building an AiForm Mining vertical (Mining Supplier Passport + opportunity/eligibility matching) on top of AiForm Procure. It compares AiForm's current capabilities and proposed mining roadmap against the three closest South African competitors identified in prior research: B1SA (now B1LINK), MineVendorHub, and SCNet. Coupa and SAP Ariba are shown as reference points only — they are mine-side enterprise systems, not direct competitors for supplier-side discovery.

No competitor owns the supplier's cross-mine journey. Mining procurement is digitised mine-by-mine (Sibanye on Coupa, Thungela on Ariba, Bushveld on SCNet, others on proprietary portals). B1SA has the deepest verification infrastructure but is buyer/compliance-led. MineVendorHub claims the closest mining-specific feature set but its market traction is unverified. SCNet has real mining-sector penetration and a large supplier directory but limited mining-charter specificity. The open space is a supplier-first eligibility layer that sits above all of these systems and routes qualified suppliers into them, rather than replacing any of them.
